utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How are you this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me also bid you good morning. I hope it won't take us long. I have two or maybe three questions for you, not more than that. Mr. Rajic, I'd like to show you now a document, ID D1/91. So will you please have a look and provide some explanations for the Court? And please, whenever you have a document, it needs to be identified, so please give us the date, who signed it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, thank you for your kind words this morning, for your words of welcome. I confirm that this document, which is authentic, is also my letter in my capacity of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in which I replied to the head of the main -- head of the staff of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Sefer Halilovic. This is in reply to his letter in which he insinuates that I personally, and General Milivoj Petkovic, head of the main staff of the HVO, and even General Janko Bobetko, head of the main staff, Chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian Army, to make it clear, the army of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us which day bears this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 14th of April, 1993. I signed the letter and notified about it, the President of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Izetbegovic, the President of the Croat community Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Mate Boban and the main staff of the Croat Defence Council. However, it is a long letter and I'd like to -- I'd like to ask Your Honours how much -- to what extent may I comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Through my questions, will you please tell us what kind of responsibility is insinuated or what kind of responsibilities on your part is he referring to? Will you please explain it and give us the concise answer as to what this is about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this is about is that Mr. Halilovic voices his concern about the possible fall of surrounded towns in east Bosnia, such as Srebrenica, Zepa and Gorazde. He suggests that I, as the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Bobetko, that we are, according to him, responsible because we had failed to ensure the passage of a rather large convoy of armament and materiel which at that time, because of the clashes between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, had been stopped at Grude. But this accusation is factually incorrect in at least two aspects. First, Mr. Halilovic knows that I cannot have that much say in the release of that convoy, just as I could not have any say with regard to his conduct. And secondly, he did not need weaponry to defend those areas in east Bosnia. He needed it to store it with other purpose in mind, in central Bosnia, in the town of Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I see -- I mean this document is self explanatory but I nevertheless see that in some ten items, you expounded certain views, certain points, for Mr. Halilovic's benefit. Will you please tell us in a nutshell what is it that you drew his attention to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be as brief as possible. I will not describe the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we object to this testimony on the grounds that it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to show us the relevance of those questions. Maybe because we don't understand the language, so we don't see the point of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before you ask any questions, could you ask the interpreter to translate certain paragraphs that related to your question? I mean, you or the witness may read certain paragraphs that is related to your question so that we could know what you are talking about, because we are totally at a loss.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. President. I thought that the document had been translated. My sincere apologies. Now, I realise now it has just occurred to me that these documents have not been translated yet. Your Honours, this is highly relevant because this is the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina writing to the Chief of Staff of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the date is the 14th of April, 1993. First, this letter proves that they were still receiving armaments from the HVO. He is then warned about all the incidents, to begin with, there was -- there were these armaments which went towards the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Secondly, the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in ten items, warns the head of the armed forces about all the omissions, of all the failures, which have produced conflicts and which have given rise to conflicts and now I think perhaps it would be best if I read this item by item. It is not long. And it won't take much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, we object to this procedure. Counsel's description of a document is very helpful but it's no substitute for a translation. It is a lengthy document, Mr. President, and it would take a fair amount of time for us to read this or to ask the interpreters to read it for us. And based on what we do know about it, it is our submission that the matters that are discussed or dealt with in this letter are irrelevant or are largely marginal to the issues that are central to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no, I cannot accept that. No, there is no way I can accept this. Whenever the Prosecutor does not like, they say it is irrelevant. Excuse me but if it is irrelevant, then the BH Army under your command continues to evidently interfere with political issues, and uses numerous activities to plan, provoke and carry out armed conflicts, with HVO units, in spite of the public appeal of the president of the Presidency, Mr. Izetbegovic, not to do that, and in spite of the peace plan signed in New York. B: Your personal order to the commander of the 4th Corps of 28th of January, 1993, is irrefutable proof of your interference in fundamental political issues. C: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina arbitrarily suspends provisional bodies of the executive authority. The executive authority of the HVO in some municipalities, although it had been agreed a long time ago, at the highest political level. And sets out to establish its own authority in individual municipalities which is a political and legal precedent. D: The BH Army continues with movements, with demonstration, with a show of force, with the introduction of -- with the transportation of new forces from outside, so that today, in the territory -- in the area of central Bosnia and in the Neretva valley, it has amassed some 25.000 troops. Why? And to what end? E: Members of the BH Army and the police forces of the BIH, the police forces of BIH, isn't it, are isolating localities with Croat population, removing and burning Croat national flags, intercepting, beating and disarming Croats, detaining the members of the HVO as well as civilians. F: Members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina seize from the HVO and civilians: weapons, gear, food, fuel. G: By night, around localities, fire from small arms is opened. There is a growing event that lead to frequent powerful detonations, all sorts of sabotage groups are infiltrated. The media campaign against the Croat people is continued and escalated and intensified against the Croat people, the HZ HB, the HVO, HDZ, and prominent officials of the Croat people and threatening statements are made. Armament and materiel sent to East Bosnia are diverted and stored in Visoko and at the same time, media are used to spread the lie that this was done by the Kiseljak HVO. The listed phenomena, such as I have presented them, as they were presented to me in the HVO on the basis of reports received, I will also illustrate with the help of -- with the support of facts as to the scene of the incident, time and content. The so-called mayor of the municipalities of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, Mr. Safet Cibo, said on the 12th of April, 1993, speaking for the local radio station, that the BH Army will be in Prozor whether one likes it or not. He accuses Croats of the genocide over the Muslims, draws a sign of equality between the HZ HB with the so-called Republika Srpska, denies the HVO legitimacy, and resists the agreed peace -- the peace plan agreed in New York. On the 8th of April, 1993, in Travnik, members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina took down and burnt -- took [indiscernible] down and burned Croatian flags, beat members of the command of the HVO Travnik Brigade, and to all this, the 3rd corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is not in the text. The interpreters comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- from Zenica responds with a protest claiming that the Croatian flags may be hoisted only on religious objects, because they allegedly are a provocation or tease members of other peoples. On the Easter day, that is the 11th of April, 1993, fire was opened on the command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's right, operative zone, central Bosnia. And the media overtly refer to Croats as fascists, war criminals and the like. This -- and there is a number -- there is a whole series of other incidents like this one and proposals how to prevent it. There are proposals concerning cooperation, agreement. I don't want to waste your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, my question to the witness is: Did you write this? Did you appeal to his common sense so that, together, you could stop these incidents and continue your common struggle and so on?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the question as leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I understand that you told me that the matters discussed and dealt with in this letter is irrelevant and much not to this case. So since we don't know the contents of this document, I believe that I'll let the Defence counsel go for a while, to see where he's leading us. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So just the answer to this question: Is that the content of this document? Did you write all that I've just read, and briefly, what else did you warn him about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, to show that there is some sense to the first part of the letter, it is necessary to read several items, which I suggested and what I requested from the chief of the main staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Halilovic. So if I may, Your Honours, what I did suggest and ask is as follows: "Do you -- if you want to save Srebrenica and other vulnerable areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina, if you want to save them, show us that you are willing to establish a sincere and responsible relationship, cooperation and realisation of fulfilment of the commitments undertaken. If your intentions are honourable, and if you want me, among others, to be up to the presumed authority of the person and function as written, then I must request from you to immediately: 1: Issue orders and enforce sanctions to forbid the interference of units under your command in political affairs. 2: To sanction severely when officers and soldiers of the army of BH make statements which are inflammatory and which incite hatred between Croats and Muslims. 3: Order -- to order the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina to strictly respect political agreements between the authorised representatives of the peoples and in particular commitments undertaken under the peace plan. 4: To prohibit movement, provocation and put an immediate end to hostilities, first in Konjic, but also in all the other lands. 5: To prevent arrests, seizure of weapons, gear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you, and I apologise particularly to the witness for interrupting him. It's not the witness's job to make sure that translations are in the courtroom. He's now on item number 4 of what appear to be 12 items. We are going to spend the morning reading this letter and that's a procedure that we object to. This is no way to work, Mr. President. If this is such an important letter written by the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it's my submission that this letter could and should have been translated long before these proceedings this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, I quite agree with you, Mr. Stringer. I did not expect this letter, which is so long, and I think we arrived at agreement that if the document is short and concise, we will use it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. temporarily without translation, but it seems to me that this letter is very long and involves some important issues in it, and we are in a very awkward position, to judge this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can continue but when the document has been translated, it will be self explanatory and Your Honours will be able to appreciate the significance of the letter. It is I think not important at this point in time to continue the -- this examination of this document. We outlined the most important ones. Yesterday we had an important meeting and agreement and I should like to thank for the conclusions reached there, both to Your Honours and the registry. So I will continue with your permission, Your Honours. This is my one but last question. This is -- this refers to document ID D1/94. The date is the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, would you please answer the first question? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very briefly, can you tell us what does this document refer to and who was it signed by?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document that has just for the first time been provided to the Prosecution. It's only in the native tongue of the witness. I can't read it, and again for all the reasons I've already said this morning, we object to this procedure and we object to counsel's use of this document during this direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I'm surprised to hear that this is the first time for the Prosecution to read this document. I believe at the very beginning of this trial, we made an order. Whatever document in your possession which you are going to use or tender during the trial should be furnished to the Prosecution long before the direct examination starts. This is the ruling we made at the very beginning of this trial. In the direct examination, there should be no surprise attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not attacking, in terms of surprise, nor is the Prosecution surprised. They are behaving like a spoiled brat. Yesterday, although the witness -- may I be allowed, Your Honours? I can not continue to work like that. Then I will ask you for a continuation of one month to have all the documents translated, not allowing the Prosecutor to, whenever they feel this is good for them, to file an appeal, whenever they do not, I really submitted to him everything, everything I had in Croatian, in Chinese and all the languages and the learned friend knew of my difficulties. I was expecting some understanding and collegiate help. The Prosecution did not have all the documents. Now what is the problem if the documents had been translated, he would probably have been surprised again, and although yesterday, the witness said the solemn declaration and then of course, some of the documents were also handed in only in the past, only a few minutes before 9.00 and in order to catch me at a surprise, and now we are hearing all these complaints. It turns out that the Prosecution can do whatever they want. We cannot do anything. And whatever the Prosecution insists upon is granted. We are -- have all the difficulties and of course everybody is in a difficult situation and you will have noticed the great pain we went through in order to observe the schedule and your requests. I do apologise, Your Honours. Perhaps this was an emotional outbreak and I should like to apologise to the learned friend as well but this was from my heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are all aware of the difficulties that one encounters prosecuting and defending cases here. However, we don't want everything. We only want what we are entitled to. We only want a fair hearing. We only want the ability to conduct a fair cross-examination of defence witnesses and I can't do it when I'm -- when a document is dropped on me ten minutes before cross-examination starts that's in a language that I can't read. And that's the point. It's not about what I would like or what I want or what I demand. It's what I'm entitled to as a party to this proceeding, and that's we are asking for, Mr. President, and until we have a translation that we can use to conduct the effective cross-examination that we are entitled to, then we will object and we will continue to object, to documents being provided to us in a language which is not one of the working languages of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there is two issues involved. The first one is the translation. I believe this Trial Chamber has done its utmost to facilitate the work of the translation. I've entrusted the Registrar to get in touch with the parties, with the translation sections, and ask them to do their utmost to finish this work of translation in time; otherwise, it will be a major obstacle to the proceedings of this trial. In this point, I agree with both parties. And maybe the Registrar will share with us some information about the translation issues.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yesterday, we had a meeting, myself, Mark Dubuisson, Mr. Krsnik and Nika Pinter regarding the documents and we've come to the following conclusions. The first thing is that we've located, allocated the documents in terms of priority, so the Defence checked the documents, they gave us the things that were absolutely urgent and they were immediately sent to translation, to Ms. Christina Zoric who understands the priority and the urgency of this matter and she will do her utmost to translate those documents immediately and give them to us as their translated. And that also includes the documents that have been tendered during the last couple of weeks. Secondly, Mr. Krsnik and Nika Pinter were allowed, I believe, 75 hours to have towards translation. They will have a person in Croatia who is licensed and recognised by the Tribunal to translate the documents. So they also have that working at the same time as our translation unit will be working as well. And they will continue to give us the priority documents dealing with witnesses that will be coming in the next weeks, and we believe that if we move in this way we will facilitate the trial and make sure that the documents are in the courtroom while the witness is being examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second issue is the obligation under the Rules of Procedure, namely, the obligation of disclosure. As this Trial Chamber ruled at the very beginning of this trial, as well as at the very beginning of the Defence case, direct examination is totally different with the cross-examination. In the case of direct examination, the party has the obligation to disclose all the documents to the other party, long before the trial, no matter whether it's the -- the document has been translated or not. In the direct examination, the surprise attack is not allowed. But things are quite different in cross-examination. In cross-examination, we only need the list of those documents before cross-examination, so that to facilitate the proceedings of the cross-examination. If this document is not furnished to the other party long beforehand, in the direct examination, this document is forbidden to use during the direct examination. Is that clear, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clear, Your Honour. Whereby I would like to emphasise that the Prosecutor did not disclose all the documents either and we do not have an agreement concerning the disclosure, and I would receive from the Prosecutor documents one day in advance or in the morning of the day when the direct examination was started. This is what was going on. Except of course for the documents which are supporting material which I had received prior to the start of the trial. I will not be using this document, Your Honours, because of these difficulties. Of course, I'll tender this into my filings once it was translated, but I would now like to put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was Mr. Arif Pasalic or another BIH army commander abiding by this famous order of the 16th of January of 1993? And if so, what was their response?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I must say that the command of no unit to which this order refers officially replied to me. They behaved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, I apologise for the interruption. I assume that we are talking about the order issued by the witness on the 16th of January, 1993, the one that he talked about yesterday. Counsel referred to the famous order and I just want to make sure that's the order that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's a legitimate request. Mr. Krsnik, you may have it clarified for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means. Well, Mr. Rajic signed only one order of the 16th of January, 1993, which was based on the Vance-Owen Plan, and this is the only order that was signed. This is D1/90, DD1/90 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, with your permission, may the witness continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. So the command, both military and civilian of no single army component to which the order referred officially answered at no time. I am familiar with the fact that the military command of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, through their individual orders, such as this one, which was signed by the commander of the 4th Corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Arif Pasalic, in fact a clear message that somebody else is the commander of these components. This is putting it in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question, I'm referring to P100 document. Fortunately we have this document translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please bring the document forward?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krsnik. In translation the response which your witness made doesn't really make sense. It's a bit cryptic. Mr. Arif Pasalic -- in fact a clear message that somebody else is the commander of these components. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you answer the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how this sounded but what I said was the following: Officially, no party ever provided me with an answer. However, the individual orders, which were given by the commanders of the BIH army, and this one is one of those, the one signed by Mr. Pasalic, represents a clear message that they will refuse to execute my orders and that they have others to -- whose orders they will follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who are those others?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are the chief of the main staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at that time Mr. Sefer Halilovic, and the civil commander of the BiH army, the President of the Presidency, Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's much clearer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I have just been reminded to make the transcript clear. You said that the individual orders and this order is one of those. Are you referring to the document when you are using the phrase, "This order"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring to the order given by the commander of the 4th Corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was the substance of the order, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To continue with certain preparations, with a view of improving the combat readiness. Then a specific prohibition to follow the decisions, as it is said here, of the HVO, HZ HB. Then to refrain from any provocation, continued reporting on measures. This is the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So that we know what the order you were referring to. Mr. Rajic, my last question. You have document P100 in front of you. My first question, are you familiar with Mr. Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Mr. Kljujic was the President of my party, the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, until February, 1992, for about two years he was president of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In what mode and for what reasons did he leave the party, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He withdrew from his office at a meeting of the central board of the party, which was held in Siroki Brijeg, under the pressure of serious criticism because of his passive attitude, lack of undertaking the necessary measures to prepare his people to defend themselves from the aggression, and because of a subordinate position that he had imposed upon the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina towards the democratic action party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When he was the President, what was the social and political system that he was advocating, in terms of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As president of the party, he could not advocate for a programme which would be in opposition to the programme of the party as a whole. Therefore, he too, as one of the officials, advocated a restructuring of Yugoslavia to make it into a loose confederation. When this was no -- not possible, he advocated the sovereignty and independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a clearcut internal system and structure which would respect the fact that Bosnia and Herzegovina as a state is a state of three constituent peoples. I apologise. I would like to finish my sentence. Although Mr. Kljujic enjoys the reputation of somebody who is infatuated with Bosnia and Herzegovina or as this is usually referred to, he is a pro-Bosnia oriented person. He too, following the aggression on Ravno in southeast Bosnia-Herzegovina, following a practical Serb secession in Bosnia and Herzegovina, started to understand that an internal division of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as a final definitive division of Bosnia and Herzegovina would be a better solution than bloodshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, would you please focus on the last paragraph of the interview in Novi List by Mr. Kljujic, the date is 13th October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document please be put on the ELMO? I have just been reminded that I have to repeat the number of the document time and again, but I'm reading document P100, the last paragraph of it, which somewhere in the middle, he says, "So the division of Bosnia is unavoidable. Unfortunately over the last 45 years, we have been displaced."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the text, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the war, they were 25 per cent, 25 per cent of the population were Croats, now there are only 17 per cent.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the document be placed on the ELMO, please, because the interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "However, I believe that there are no more possibilities for a common life and that it would be fair for us to be divided -- to divide ourselves and to carry out a transfer of population. This would be a painstaking and painful effort and it will cause a great deal of trauma, but this perhaps is better than living within this atmosphere of hatred." I wanted to read out only this paragraph because I thought it was an interesting one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recall this interview? Did you have any conversation with him in connection with this interview?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recall this interview. And I can also recall that it was fiercely attacked by the media of Sarajevo, which perhaps was the reason of indecision that Kljujic later manifested and he, perhaps for this reason, tried to distance himself from these statements. At that time, I did not occupy a high political position, and I did not often get an opportunity to communicate with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, could we have the date of that interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, October 13th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, I think that it is important for Their Honours to hear a very short passage from the last paragraph. In this interview, at the end of it, Mr. Kljujic says as follows: "However, after everything that had happened, the division of Bosnia is the only way out. And I think that Serbs will have to separate their territories and their people. We will make a suggestion to the Muslims that in the remaining parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we continue to live together as a community and that as a confederation, we link up with Slovenia and Croatia or to be fully independent. "Should they" -- he's referring to the Muslims, "decide not to accept this, then we too will ask to have our own part." The rest, I think, is not of particular importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I want to bring this examination to a close. Can you just tell us were these personal views of Mr. Kljujic or were they the official stands and position of the party and which was the personal and which was the official? If you are familiar with that, of course.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a person holds a public office and if in this case it is the President of a party, then that person invariably speaks on behalf of the party unless this is -- this possibility is explicitly excluded. To these views, one needs to remind of these -- Mr. Kljujic's views precisely because one needs to see how, in all that political and military nightmare which was lying heavily on my homeland, Bosnia-Herzegovina, it shows how one had to think, one had to bear in mind every variation, every possibility. If somebody is in love with Bosnia-Herzegovina, if somebody is in love with the statehood and Mr. Kljujic is indubitably one of those, if such a person has been cornered and realised that the partition, the division was the only way out, then this is a reflection of all that the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina did, thought and said, in order to save themselves from the looming war disaster, and that is why I think it is important that we remind ourselves of the way in which the President Kljujic thought at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is Bosnia-Herzegovina still divided?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I remind you that yesterday, my answers, I said that the Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a leading party, the HDZ, had accepted all the peace agreements down to the last one, realising that none of them was governed by justice and fairness, and the present -- the current agreement, which underpins the present Bosnia-Herzegovina is indubitably an unfair agreement, which, if I may put it that way, which has put two souls in one half of a body and gave another soul a whole body. This is unfair. This is not ethical but I hope that a time will redress this injustice and that we shall arrive at the natural state of things, that all the peoples have equal rights and equal solutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic. This was my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I realise that you make -- made your direct examination within the time limit. We are not satisfied that this morning; we wasted a lot of time. Well, I understand it's not entirely your fault. It's about the translation. Well, Mr. Stringer, could we have our break a little bit earlier and resume earlier so that you could continue the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a good idea, Mr. President. During the break we will make sure that any new exhibits have been distributed. I think they have already been distributed to counsel, as well as a list of any witnesses we intend to use during the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will resume at 20 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Bring in the witness, please. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, good morning. My name is Douglas Stringer. I'll be asking you questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, first about the various positions you held at the various times, particularly during 1991, 1992, and 1993. If I understand correctly, you held a variety of positions in the political party known as the Croatian Democratic Union; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Except that my political advancement was gradual, from the lowest to the highest. During those years that you mention in your question, I did not hold any high-ranking political post.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll try to ask you a series of short questions about that. Hopefully you'll be able to give me short answers although I certainly don't want to you feel that you can't give full answers. You became involved with the HDZ in latter -- in the latter part of 1990, I believe, just prior to the multi-party elections; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes, on the 12th of June, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And subsequently, then in the autumn of 1990 [sic], in November, throughout what was then the former Yugoslavia, multi-party elections were held; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think you quoted the wrong year. It was in 1990, sometime in mid-November.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. And in the multi-party elections, then, at the time of the multi-party elections, in the fall of 1990, you were a local HDZ representative in the municipality of Kupres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you did not word it properly. I was not a representative. I was the President of the municipal board of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina in my municipality in Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At some point, you became vice-president of the HDZ party for Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was much later. I believe at the fourth convention of our party, when Mr. Dario Kordic was elected president of your party.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate date when you became vice-president of the HDZ BH?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the 3rd of July, 1995. But I'm not quite sure about the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So through 1990 through -- through June of 1995, your only position in the HDZ was as a local, or I should say, president of the municipal board for Kupres?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a member of some central party bodies too, and during a term, I was a member of the central board of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and before my election as the vice-president of our party, I was a member of the executive board of that party, and it is the executive body of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's not important for us to get the titles precisely. Would it be correct for me to say that during latter -- the latter part of 1991, 1992, and 1993, you held a position of some responsibility and some leadership within the HDZ party of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wouldn't be accurate, because the leading functions in the party are with the Presidency, and at that time, I was at no time a member of the Presidency of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the latter part of 1991, did you attend meetings in various locations, regional meetings of the various boards in places such as Grude, Tomislavgrad, perhaps other places?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now and then. But only in the capacity that I had, and which was the only one that I had and that was the President of the municipal board.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In addition, in latter 1991, did you attend meetings in Zagreb with members of the HDZ for the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I attended one such meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And is that the meeting which -- in which President Tudjman received you and others who had come up from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Tudjman received a delegation of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not me. I was merely one -- a member of this delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were present at the meeting with President Tudjman, though.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just for the Trial Chamber's information, this is later, and it's beyond the time frame that we are concerned with for this case, but it's my understanding that ultimately, I believe later in 1995 or 1996, you assumed the position of president of the HDZ for Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be more correct to say on the 16th of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this is the same position that had previously been held by Stjepan Kljujic, Milenko Brkic, Mate Boban, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you also testified yesterday that at some point for a period of time, you held the position of Minister of Defence for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe your testimony was that you held that position from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. latter part of 1992 until sometime in the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be more accurate if I say, as I said yesterday, end of 1992 until mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is it possible, sir, that you formally held the position of Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina for a longer period of time, until the fall, say October, of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I have a report, and I can show it to you, I only have it in English, from the Sarajevo Radio which indicates that on the 18th of October, 1993, you and others were relieved of your duties within the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the same of course applies to me. I am asking for the document to be translated so that it is all fair and just and so that the witness can read it. Everything else I consider unfair and unjust and as an attempt to set a trap for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution is just asking a question about the time when he finished his job as the Minister of Defence. Let's hear what the witness answers. If you need -- if you need that document, I believe that the Prosecutor will furnish it to you, but it all depends on how the proceedings go. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think counsel's point is well taken. I don't intend to tender this, this report, it's just something which I have and have read, suggesting that Mr. Rajic was at least in some capacity, still a member of the Bosnia-Herzegovina government until October of 1993. I'm simply using that, asking him whether that's correct or not correct. I don't intend to offer the article itself. So it's simply the basis of my asking him the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, I shall be happy to answer your question. We are all clear that there is meritorious evidence and there is speculation. This document, with which you wanted to acquaint me is a media speculation and I'm quite confident about that. What is valid is the decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which relieved me of that duty in July, the duty of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So there is no way in which I could continue holding that office without authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll ask the usher to provide the witness with two exhibits at this time. I believe they are both new ones, Exhibit 159.1 and 236.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, now we are going to move away from the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I want to ask you now some questions about positions you held within the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO. And maybe while we are waiting for the document, I can ask you a couple of preliminary questions. It's my understanding, sir, that in July of 1992, you were appointed to a position in the HVO as an assistant for information and propaganda activities of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact is correct, but your wording is not correct. I was not responsible for propaganda but for information and political activity, and I was the spokesman of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you were appointed by Mate Boban; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we are looking at Exhibit 159.1. Sir, does this appear to be the document in which you were appointed to this position that we have been discussing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I don't speak and read your language. The translation that I've been given for the title, IPD, I've been given the words, "Information, propaganda activities for the main staff of the HVO." Could you -- do you agree with me that that would be a correct description of the title that you were appointed to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not an accurate description of my position. We did not have a service that would be responsible for propaganda. We had a service which was responsible for information and political activity, like any other army. But it wasn't governed by propaganda principles and I was the port parole, I was the spokesman and it was very important to mention who transmitted official views of the defence department and the main staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you transmitted these official views to the media, to other persons or organisations who were seeking information from the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to Mr. Stringer. Mr. Sheric now warns me that we again have a problem with interpretation, that our distinguished interpreters keep saying propaganda even though the witness did not say propaganda. In the document, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think the witness has explained that sufficiently. We can argue about what the document says or doesn't say but I believe the witness has been given a fair opportunity to describe the position himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it cannot be in the translation -- but it wasn't governed by the propaganda principles because the witness did not say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there is different understandings and interpretations concerning the word "propaganda" in different cultures. We must accept that as a fact. Secondly, Mr. Stringer, in order to make the transcript clear, you may ask this question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I ask the usher to put the B/C/S version of the document on the ELMO so that the interpreters -- although I believe they have it themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajic, I'm looking at what for me are the words "assistant for information-propaganda activities at the HVO headquarters." Now, it seems to me that the operative letters here are IPD. Could you tell us what IPD stands for, since you held this position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, an acronym is used here which then lends itself to different interpretations, but I know, because of the content, what it means and I also know what it means formally. This is the information and political activity. And will you please be so kind and put it like that in the record? Propaganda in our Croatian language has a negative connotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll accept that, Mr. President, and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I merely wish to say that this is very arbitrary and I've come across many such documents and this is a very arbitrary interpretation because in the Croatian original, it says IPD and in English translation, the information and propaganda activities. I don't know where did the translators get this because that is not in the Croatian document, and I wish to warn that there is a whole series of documents which we received from the Prosecution where it -- where this -- we find the same mistake and that is not permissible. The translators could have put their IPD and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that if the translation or interpreter makes mistakes, everybody will notice the existence, but if they did not make any mistakes, we have the intention to forget them at all. Mr. Krsnik, you have the right to raise any misinterpreted or translated words in the documents or in the interpretations during the proceedings, but I believe this issue has been solved. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, do you have the next exhibit in front of you? That would be P236.8. That's a document dated the 31st of January, 1993. Now, sir, this is a document signed by Bruno Stojic, who is the head of the defence department for the HVO, in which he proposes your dismissal from the position which I believe that we've just been discussing. Is that a fair characterisation of this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You put it correctly. This relief of duty was necessary because I had already been appointed the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and it was advisable for me to cease holding any posts in the HVO. And it needed to be resolved in a formal -- in the formal manner also, even though I had stopped discharging these responsibilities even before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, sir, that on the date that you issued the order for the units of the TO to disarm in Vance-Owen cantons 3, 8 and 10, on the 16th of January, 1993, you continued to hold this position as a spokesperson responsible for information and political affairs of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is -- there is always a possibility for an administrative error. It is quite possible that I did attend some other press conferences, but it did not change my position. At that time, I was the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if, from yesterday's testimony, if the Trial Chamber concluded that as of the end of 1992, you discontinued any activities on behalf of the HVO, then that would not be a correct statement. It would not be a correct understanding.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, yesterday I answered questions about my career, and whenever I spoke about that, I spoke about acts which produced changes in my status, so decisions on my designation, on my appointment of my moving from one office to the other, and I see no inconsistency there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So sir, in fact, during January of 1993, you held both positions, that is a position as Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina and also at the same time, you continued to hold the position within the HVO involved in political information and acting as a spokesman. Would that be a fair statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think one could put it that way, because I handed over the duties gradually to one of my assistants, Mr. Veso Vegar and from time to time, I insisted -- I helped in the exercise of some duties, but as for my terms of reference, as for my field of operation, I could not do it any longer in the HVO, bearing in mind the duty that we have just talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of an assistant. It's not appearing correctly on the transcript. Are we talking about Veso Vegar?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is he the person who followed you after you finally and officially resigned or no longer held the position within the HVO that we have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of my assistants, whilst I was the spokesman, and directly responsible for information, and I was helping him -- I helped him to become acquainted with what the job involved and to take it over from me eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, in connection with your order of 16 January, 1993, we will talk about it more later, but in fact, after you issued that order and after it was reported in the media, did you not explain your views in respect of that order in both of your capacities as a Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina but also in your capacity as a spokesperson for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I was a person who was very much exploited by the media. My press conferences were broadcast several times a day, so with no undue modesty, I must say that for the Croats and for Muslims, I was that voice of encouragement that made people come to me and thank me for encouraging them, for boosting their spirits in such a convincing -- in such a persuasive manner. And that is why it is very difficult to show it to people -- it's very difficult to make people aware that I'm no longer that person, that spokesperson, and that I'm now appearing in a different role, and I do not exclude the possibility that the two could be confused in the perception of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During this period, late 1991, early 1992, where were you based, physically? Sarajevo? Mostar? A different place? Kupres?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the year, please? I think you misquoted the year. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We spoke a few moments ago about the latter part of 1991.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I lived in Kupres throughout, so then too in the latter part of 1991, I was in Kupres, and I was there until the war broke out, in Kupres, rather, the all-out war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And when my municipality was occupied, I moved to work in Grude and then on to Mostar, and my family was displaced and went to Basko Polje, near Makarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were one of the many refugees who went down to Mostar after your own municipality was taken over by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately, I was one of many refugees but I did not go to Mostar straight away. I arrived there in late July, 1992, but I never lived in Mostar during the war. I never spent a night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During the period in which you were Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you work in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that was not possible. I mean, it is -- that it is common knowledge that Sarajevo was under a terrible siege, that one could enter it or get out of it only at high risk, and a little later, through an improvised tunnel. So the rest of the government in Sarajevo had to work under impossible conditions and that was the decisive point. That is why I could not -- I could never go there during my term of office. Although, I think that it would have been better had it in line with the decisions of the highest authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, had the government and the wartime Presidency and all the other bodies been moved to other locations, but that was not done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to come back to the HDZ party. Correct me if I'm wrong. In the multi-party elections of November 1990, the leading parties, the most successful parties were the HDZ, the SDS, and the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On behalf of the HDZ, which was the Croat affiliated party, two persons who gained the most votes were Stjepan Kljujic and Franjo Boras; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Because of that, those two Croats became members of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In addition, at this time, and throughout 1991, Stjepan Kljujic was also the President of the HDZ for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Stjepan --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. He, as the President, also was the candidate to become a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Stjepan Kljujic, as you moved through 1990 into 1991, tended to favour a policy, a solution for Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was more closely linked to the Muslims and to an independent, undivided Bosnia-Herzegovina. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I must add something. All of us in HDZ, me included, were in favour of the same policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at some point, however, the policy of Kljujic and the policy of others within the HDZ, perhaps including yourself, began to diverge. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say whether diverge is the right word to use, but the differences in terms of views as to which of the problems that we were surrounded by, and in terms of the models through which this can be resolved did exist, which, within a democratic party, is quite a normal and usual phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And on the side opposing Kljujic's views were persons such as Mate Boban, Franjo Boras, and yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot accept this characterisation and the names offered. But we cannot speak about opposition on the part of Mr. Kljujic. We were still on the same side. Our discussions arose out of a lack of agreement concerning preparations for the defence, and concerning the awareness that the war can be avoided or cannot be avoided. We could be divided into those who wanted active intervention and those who thought that they can be just second-hand actors to the Party of Democratic Action. This was the substance of our difference of views.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you about your own views. And let's focus on the period of late 1991. Say around the time that you went to Zagreb with the others and met with President Tudjman. Let's talk about your views during that period of time. You spoke yesterday about what attracted you, even at the beginning, to the HDZ party. You spoke of reconciliation of the Croatian people. I believe you spoke about the potential for establishing a Croatian or a Croat entity or state. Now, those are objectives which differed from the objectives of Kljujic, who was in more favour of a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina, more closer linkage to the Muslims. Would you agree with me on that point?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I must admit that it is with a high degree of skill that you have put the same facts into two different contexts. Namely, I said that I supported the programme based objective of the Croatian Democratic Union that applied to the entire territory of Yugoslavia and not only to Bosnia-Herzegovina, which sought a restructuring of Yugoslavia to make it a confederation. And I also said that I supported and endorsed the political option of HDZ, that should this prove to be impossible to achieve, to focus upon the independence of the Republic of Croatia, which has no linkage whatsoever with Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I'd like to recall everybody concerned the third fact, that is linked to this party, is its attitude towards Bosnia-Herzegovina, and its programme, which supports and endorses the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the rights vested in the constitutive peoples, but which, not under the most adverse circumstances, will not leave the Bosnian Croats, Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as we usually say, unattended and unhelped. I think Mr. Prosecutor that it's very important for these two notions to be separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Focusing now, again, on the period of late 1991, would you agree with me, sir, that by that period of time, it was pretty evident to everyone that war was unavoidable?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct answer would be that the majority, the majority of the Croats were aware of it. There were people, however, who never understood the threat of war, but these were a minority, a very small minority indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And by the end of 1991, you and others in the HDZ had decided that your best option was the establishment of a Croatian entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or even better, incorporation or accession into a Republic of Croatia. Wasn't that your goal, your objective by the end of 1991 to become part of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct at all. I'll be very frank and open. I am not a novice in political affairs and I also have a certain degree of general knowledge, but in Croatian knowledge, the word "entity" cropped up only after Dayton. Before Dayton, it had no meaning whatsoever and no significance. Therefore, it would be senseless indeed to claim that we were working towards the establishment of something that one could refer to it as an entity. Furthermore, even less correct would be the claim that at that time we decided to accede or to become a part of the Republic of Croatia. This in terms of facts is not true. There is evidence, there is document that one cannot interpret in this sense, and they serve as an evidence per se.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will ask the usher be given IAC-2 and Exhibit P104.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Rajic: Dario Kordic, Mate Boban, by the end of 1991, didn't they want to establish Croatian territory in Bosnia and to make that territory part of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can speak about my own deeds, and I can speak about the events that took place in those localities in which I was present. Overstepping this ethical boundary of speech and evaluation and judgement is unacceptable to me, and I would not like to offer any comment as to the deeds and acts and particularly the thoughts that were harboured by other people. Except when they are also contained in a political decision, but that's another question, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the document IAC-2. These are the conclusions of a joint meeting of Herzegovina regional community and the Travnik regional community. This was held, I believe, in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991. Sir, take a moment to look this document over.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It may assist to put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you something.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before you ask me, I have a request. The document in front of me, in no way whatsoever can be considered an authentic document. It is not a signed document. The three persons mentioned did not sign it. There is no seal. And I really cannot offer any thoughts in connection with a document like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's just use it as an aid to assist further questioning. Were you at a meeting in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991? A meeting of membership of the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, Mr. Prosecutor, I have to share with you my displeasure with the fact that you are offering me, even though it's done in a haphazard manner, unauthenticated documents. As far as the meeting in Grude is concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to ask the President's assistance in directing the witness just to answer the question. I think if the Trial Chamber has any concerns about the manner in which the cross-examination is being conducted, the Trial Chamber will step in. Beyond that, I'd simply ask you to instruct the witness to answer what is a simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, just put aside whether this document is authentic or not. The Prosecution is asking you about a very simple question, and you have to answer that question. The document is just kind of an aid to you. You may just put it aside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. What I wanted to say, having been asked by the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not want to protect the witness. I want to voice an objection of the manner in which he is being cross-examined by the Prosecutor because if this document or any other document which is being forwarded to the witness is in no relation whatsoever with the question or questions to be asked, then why in the first place is the document being forwarded to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to request Their Honours to perhaps, before any document is tendered in or submitted by the Prosecutor, to ask the Prosecutor to tell us what the document is all about so that the witnesses are not confused and would not react in the manner we have just witnessed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution is asking a very, very simple question, that is, were you at a meeting on the 12th in a certain place in a certain date. It's a very simple question. And this is the cross-examination, Mr. Krsnik. I believe this document is in your possession long, long ago, and I believe this document has been admitted into evidence already. Yes, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be allowed to say one sentence? I cannot answer the Prosecutor's question whether I was at this meeting or not, if the evidence does not provide enough foundation for us to establish that the meeting took place in the first place. However, if the meeting took place, I cannot recall whether I participated in it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you just tell what you know about this meeting. If you don't remember that meeting, you just tell us, "I don't remember there is a meeting there." It's a very simple issue. It's not so complicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the question is: Were you at that meeting at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said before, Your Honours, I cannot recall my being there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then I believe the Prosecutor may refresh your memory by providing some materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, just so I'm being as precise as I should be, a meeting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the presidents of the Crisis Staffs, the Herzegovina regional community, presidents and representatives of the Crisis Staffs of the Travnik regional community, was held on the 12th of November, 1991, in Grude. The meeting was chaired by Mate Boban. Dario Kordic was the co-chair. Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I cannot recall it, because I was a dilettante, an amateur. I was doing my business and I don't know where exactly I was present at that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This document, sir, refers to decisions taken at that meeting in which it was decided that the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina must embrace a determined and active policy to realise our eternal dream, a common Croatian state. My question, sir, is whether that was in fact the views of the HDZ party as of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about the establishment or restoration of the boundaries of what's known as the Hrvatska Banovina from 1939? By November of 1991, wasn't it also an objective of the HDZ party in Bosnia-Herzegovina to achieve a restoration of the territory of the Croatian Banovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have knowledge of any serious political document that would treat this issue in a manner you've just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was it your own view, sir, during this period of time, November, 1991, that the Croatian -- the Hvratska Banovina provided a -- provided the territory or was the model on which boundaries, demarcation of Croatian territory should be decided?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had not arrived at all at a situation in which we would be thinking about demarcations, except for the internal one. The -- a Croatian Banovina as a political concept represents a fact of history, from which certain historical rights can be derived, but in my mind, it was not an instrument of the current policies at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at this meeting, it was also concluded that it was necessary to make better military preparations for combat against all those forces which would attempt to stop the inevitable process of the creation of a free Croatian state. I'm referring you, sir, to item C, paragraph 3 of the document. This is my question: Is it true, sir, that by this period of time, November, 1991, the leadership of the HDZ party of Bosnia-Herzegovina had decided that it would resort to military force to implement its version, its views, in establishing a Croat state on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I never confirmed it to you that these conclusions had been made. So I can refer to them as purely hypothetical. But if there were such conclusions made, then I cannot find a single place where these conclusions would imply that Bosnia and Herzegovina must also be a part of that Croatia. From this text, this interpretation cannot be made. But of course, all Croats, including myself, supported and endorsed the right of the Croat people in the then Socialist Republic of Croatia to, in a democratic manner, achieve their independence and sovereignty, since the greater Serbia project did not recognise the model of equality of rights and of a confederation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's back up, then, on that point, into paragraph 2 of this document. Isn't it not also true that in addition to restoration of a Croatian Banovina, the HDZ party in Bosnia-Herzegovina also sought and envisioned the holding of a referendum ultimately on joining the Republic of Croatia? Was that also not one of the objectives of your party in late 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I really feel insulted. You persistently are quoting to me the conclusions made at a meeting which I -- a meeting, the holding of which I could not confirm to you. I cannot answer questions which you are singling out from a document which is entirely unauthentic. Unfortunately, I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, as I said just now, you just put aside that document. I understand you challenge the authenticity of that document, which has happened. In the cross-examinations, there are always various arguments between the Prosecution, the party conducting the cross-examination, and the witness; it's quite natural. The Prosecution asked you a question whether to hold a referendum ultimately on joining the Republic of Croatia was one of the objectives of your party in later 1993. If it's yes, you just simply answer yes. If it's no, you answer no. That's very simple. I hope you could understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This was not the objective, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the next exhibit there, marked as Exhibit P104?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the sake of fairness, I believe you first said 1993 and then corrected yourself and said 1991, and this is not in the transcript. Line 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- Mr. Rajic, can you identify this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This decision results from a meeting that was held in Grude on the 18th of November, 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I believe I see your signature among those appearing on the back of this document as a representative of Kupres?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were in support of the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just one or two brief questions about this document and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna extended from western Herzegovina all the way up well into central Bosnia, encompassing, I believe, some 3 dozen municipalities, if I'm not mistaken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that it encompassed some 30 municipalities or, rather, areas of municipalities, that is not necessarily the entire municipal territories, but this does not refer to the territory, meaning perhaps the state which is the subject, a state territory, but a territory where the Croat people would establish possible forms of preparations for the joint defence, with those who were willing and ready to fight with us on our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, there were substantial numbers of Muslims living within the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
