utterances.text: Now, I'm looking at article 7 of this decision which you signed, which vests supreme authority of the community in the Presidency, the Presidency which would consist of or comprise the most senior representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal authority or presidents of the Croatian Democratic Union municipal boards. My question, sir, is, in fact, whether there was any provision by which non-Croats could participate in a meaningful way in the governance of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, given the fact that the supreme authority appears, in my reading, to be reserved only for representatives of the Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, article 7 of the decision under consideration may not be considered separately from the provisions in Article 1. So what it speaks about is not any authority in that territory but about the provisional form of organisation of the community as a political, cultural, economic and territorial entity, and its Presidency is not a body of government but the political leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And insofar as political and territorial aspects are involved, there is in fact no room for non-Croats to participate on an equal footing with Croats in this community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No norm excludes -- no provision excludes the possibility for others who want to do so to join us, to prepare for the defence to defend together with us, and that is what we did in 90 per cent of the cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you testified already that in late 1991, you attended a meeting with others, as part of a delegation that went to Zagreb and met with President Franjo Tudjman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit PT 2, presidential transcript 2. And with the Court's permission, I've got a version that's a clean version in the witness's language to which I've tabbed particular parts I want to direct his attention to. I think it would make it go much faster to use this one rather than one that has no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think the witness needs to acquaint himself with the whole document. These are very important documents. If I'm correct, these are presidential transcripts; the witness must read it through. As the -- Your Honours know, I did not ask him any questions with regard to the transcript because I do not accord much importance to this particular meeting or on the 27th of December in the socialist federal Yugoslavia but obviously I will have to do that with some witnesses. But never mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to what's been said by counsel. Characterising the evidence based on his own personal views in the presence of the witness is highly improper. And I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You're right, Mr. Stringer, and I think also Mr. Krsnik, in fairness, from my grimaces, appreciated that I was making the same point and stopped. I think we have to give Mr. Krsnik the benefit of the doubt that he's not used to the common law procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite so, Your Honour, and thank you very much. Thank you, you're quite right. My objection was that the witness should be acquainted with the whole material rather than with some fragments which the -- my learned friend wishes to serve on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, considering the schedule, we almost approach to a break. So my suggestion is, could we break here, a little bit earlier, and during that break, the witness may read that transcript? Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely acceptable, Mr. President. I've got a couple of preliminary questions before we get into the transcript, if we want to use -- I'm not sure what time we are supposed to break actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 12.00. We still have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I could use the remaining five minutes and then Mr. Rajic could take -- with the Court's permission, I could simply give him the transcript I propose to provide to him, so that he can go precisely to the areas that I want to go over with him in the cross and then he won't -- he'll be able to focus on those and anything else he wants to read during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I see no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Rajic, then, let's talk about a couple of preliminary things. Again we are still, in my outline, we are still under the category of the HDZ party. You spoke yesterday about a HDZ party that extended across boundaries or that operated throughout the republics. That's how I understood what you were saying. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did speak about it but I -- that is not how I worded it. I said that the Croat democratics union, which was founded in the Republic of Croatia in 1989, acted in terms of the programme and its statute in the territory of two then socialist republics within the framework of one state, Yugoslavia, and that is exactly what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, by 1991, you had -- you're certain that the former Yugoslavia did not exist in the same way that it existed in 1989, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise? When in 1991? Because a year is a very long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: By the end of 1991, Slovenia was no longer a part of the socialist federal Republic of Yugoslavia, correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the point of view of constitutional law, Yugoslavia still existed, because none of the republics of that former state had yet been recognised internationally. It is true that the structure was disrupted, that its life was disrupted. There were already two wars going on, that is one of them was still going on in Croatia, but unfortunately, Yugoslavia was still a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The HDZ existed in the Republic of Croatia in November of 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The HDZ existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina as of November of 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In fact, there was a fair amount of correspondence, sharing of views, between the two parties during that period of November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not two parties. It was one party with one president, one central board, one main board, one Presidency, one programme, one statute, but they acted in two different republics of the then state, and both of them adjusted to the specific conditions of life and work in their respective territories. That is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So in November of 1991, the President of the HDZ political party was Franjo Tudjman, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the party as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was the leader of the membership of the HDZ in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The whole HDZ. The entire HDZ -- he was the President of the HDZ as the planetary, as the global party because there were subsidiaries in Canada, in Switzerland, here in Germany. So the late President Franjo Tudjman was the President of this all-encompassing system and now president of the Bosnian-Herzegovina party was Stjepan Kljujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Kljujic was beneath Mr. Tudjman in the hierarchy of the unified or entire HDZ that you've been just been describing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hierarchically speaking, yes, but we enjoyed a very high degree of autonomy in our political commitments. Especially because the Republic of Croatia had already voted for its independence and it was simply pending for its international confirmation, and that fact was increasingly respected by the party leadership and notably President Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as a result of that - and this is my last question, Mr. President - as a result of Croatia's position of independence or near independence at that time as you've described, as a result of that, President Tudjman was in a position to exert enormous influence over you and other members of the HDZ party who were operating in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt that President Tudjman was a charismatic person, that he was a politician such as the Croat people has not had for the past thousand years. To us, the Croats, he exercised tremendous influence over us and I wish to assure the Honourable Court that that influence was as often and not of a positive nature. We would never have come out to the referendum of our own will. We would have lacked strength for it had it not been for the charismatic strength of the late President Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, during the break, we hope you could take some time to acquaint yourself with those documents so that we could continue the proceedings after the break. We will rise until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Bring in the witness, please. Witness, during the break, did you have time to read the document furnished by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to facilitate the procedure. I have managed to read a part of what the Prosecutor marked in this text, but I did not manage to read it all, but what is the material -- and I believe that it is the same material I read about it years ago in a book called, "Genesis of an Illusion," so this is not the first time that I see this material, if this is the same transcript that the Prosecutor claims it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stringer, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, just before the break, I was asking you about President Tudjman and his relationship to the HDZ party of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and just before the break, you said an interesting thing that I'd like to clarify. You said, "We would never have come out to the referendum of our own will. We would have lacked strength for it had it not been for the charismatic strength of the late President Tudjman." Just so the record is clear, are we talking about the referendum on independence which took place in Bosnia-Herzegovina in late February and early March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I shall be happy to explain it. It is the referendum that I meant. When I said that without that assistance by President Tudjman we would have lacked the strength, and by this I meant our need and the decision of our central board to define the referendum question in a manner which would allow to resolve the organisation and the system of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the referendum, that is, after its independence. That is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly, then, sir, that the position of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina in respect of the upcoming referendum, your position, the position of your party, is one that was determined by the fact that President Tudjman supported the referendum himself?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had a vital influence but it was we in Bosnia-Herzegovina who made the final decision in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, this is a transcript of a meeting which occurred on the 27th of December, 1991, in the offices of President Tudjman in Zagreb. You've had a chance to look over the transcript during the break, and you've already testified a bit about this meeting. Can you tell us, sir, whether in fact you were present at this meeting in Zagreb on the 27th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was this your first meeting with President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I met President Tudjman on various occasions before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when you met him on those previous occasions, what month, what year?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In official communication, I saw President Tudjman in June, 1991. That was the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And was there another time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that June meeting, with President Tudjman, and the one that we are talking about now, on the 27th of December, 1991, I have not memorised another meeting. My personal, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, on this December meeting -- actually I'm just going to change just briefly, Mr. President. If we could go back to what was marked as IAC 2, that's one of the documents that was already shown to the witness, and I think I will just have one or two brief questions about that, IAC-2. This is a document that was shown to the witness already earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We don't have it with us, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's in evidence, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: In the big binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, in the international conflict binders. Perhaps with the usher's assistance we could put it on the ELMO, then. The English version, that is, the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajic, I'm not going to try to put words in your mouth. I know this document is one you have disputed. The meeting with President Tudjman in June of 1991, did that take place in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting in June of 1991, was there a certain orientation and conclusions that were adopted in agreements with Dr. Tudjman on the 13th and 20th of June, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meeting and the same also holds true of the one held on the 27th of December, 1991. I was never sent any minutes of either of those two meetings or any other, and I do not know if anybody else was sent the minutes. So that as regards this transcript, and these conclusions, I can only speak from my memory, of course, selected -- it is necessarily selective memory because I feel much better if I talk about things that are related to me than what was said by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher just to move the document down so that we can see paragraph 1 in its entirety? I'm sorry, the other direction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you met with President Tudjman in Zagreb in June of 1991, did you discuss what should be the policy of the HDZ in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you discuss the -- well, let me just ask you to tell us what you recall of the meeting with President Tudjman in June of 1991, and what was discussed. First perhaps I should ask you to tell us who was also present?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no man who can remember everybody who was there. I know the criteria on the basis of which we were invited. It was presidents of municipal boards of the Croat Democratic Union in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Presidency of the party in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and perhaps some other officials too but I'm not quite sure about that. So that it is really difficult after all this time, to say who was present there, because -- I mean even people who are invited are not always there. So it was the case on that occasion as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This document, IAC-2 makes reference to meetings with Dr. Tudjman on the 13th and the 20th of June, 1991. Were you present at one of those meetings or both of them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one, on the 13th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I take it that certain conclusions and agreements were reached with Dr. Tudjman at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked, but I do not recall any conclusions in writing. We talked about the political disorder, the disarray, the chaos, about the war psychosis in Croatia, the danger of war for -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina and for the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Perhaps the best description would be that we were lamenting our unfortunate lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you discuss the possibility that a common Croatian state would be to the benefit of the Croatian people in both countries?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This possibility was mentioned, if all the attempts at democratisation and organisation of Yugoslavia failed and if Serbs with the help of the so-called JNA assaulted Bosnia and Herzegovina, in that situation, one had to also count with the possibility of rescuing the remains of the Croat people and their lands in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is logical that in view of the disintegration of Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, that that possible part of the Croat people would turn and go to the mother country, where else would they? But those were hypothetical discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: However, they became less hypothetical by the end of 1991, and by that, I mean that during this period, June of 1991 to December of 1991, would you agree with me that in fact it was clearer that the attempts at democratisation had failed and the Serbs, with the assistance of the JNA, had assaulted Bosnia-Herzegovina or intended to do so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was obvious, but it did not automatically produce a change in our political behaviour, except insofar as that particular task was concerned, which meant to get ready to be prepared so as not to be exposed to a genocide and complete extermination. That change was obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so that by the end of 1991, then, sir, would you agree with me that the possibility or the need to consider a common Croatian state for the Croats of both countries was even more imperative than it had been earlier in June of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Reasons for faster thinking about if what would be if. We have not yet reached that stage. We still believed that some kind of political understanding could be reached, and we hoped that the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina would not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, recognising that you haven't read the transcript word for word, the transcript of the meeting on 27 December, 1991, from the parts that you have read, are you able to tell us whether it appears to you to be an accurate reflection of things said and discussed with Dr. Tudjman on the 27th of December?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I am aware of the fact that I am speaking under oath and that I am expected to tell the truth. I shared with you some of those truths. One truth is that I attended that meeting. I spoke at that meeting. I can recall some names and their views and opinions, but not all of them. However, I cannot confirm to you that this is an authentic document, nor has it ever been established that it is. So it can be an authentic document but it cannot. It is possible that it is not. I do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not know it. The section of the document that interprets my discussion at the meeting, in terms of the substance and sense, is reflecting what I said. So this is where I can confirm the correctness of the wording but of course, that does not imply that I can offer other comments concerning this document. It had already been commented on before, of this document, namely, the authenticity of which I could not confirm. And this is an opportunity for me to correct you. I never said that the document on the meeting in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991, is not an authentic document. What I did say is that I cannot confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let me -- just to follow up on that while you've still got it in front of you. You've had the document now in front of you on a couple of occasions; you've had a chance to read it over. Are you in a position to say, sir, whether it appears that the document marked as IAC number 2 would accurately reflect discussions and things discussed in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I would like to ask you, if possible, do not insist on asking me to confirm something that I contested in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure I understand correctly what you're saying. Correct me if I'm wrong. You don't know either way whether that document is authentic or not authentic. You simply don't know because you don't remember a meeting in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the third or the fourth time, I'd like to repeat, I'm not certain, and I cannot confirm it, but I cannot claim that it is not authentic, but I cannot confirm that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'll accept that answer.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what I propose to do with the transcript is to take you to specific parts which have been marked, to give you an opportunity to address those, at the same time that we bring them to the attention of the Trial Chamber. Now, before we start, it sounds to me as though generally speaking, you can confirm the accuracy of the statements that are attributed to you in this transcript; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I had already done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, also some of what I've marked relates to reading of the minutes of an earlier meeting that had taken place in Tomislavgrad some days prior to this meeting with Dr. Tudjman. Did you see the part about the Tomislavgrad meeting in this transcript?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that part of the text, which you refer to as the transcript, which I'm not quite sure of. I was present at the meeting in Tomislavgrad. I'm familiar with the gist of the decisions or conclusions, and although in political and linguistic terms, I'm not very pleased with the minutes of the meeting held in Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We'll talk about the minutes of that meeting in a moment. Then what I understand you're saying is that -- let me ask you this: The minutes of the Tomislavgrad meeting were read out to President Tudjman by Ignac Kostroman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I can recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's go directly to the transcript now. I've got some passages that I want to direct your attention to. First of all, for what -- you would be tab number 1 and with the usher's assistance perhaps we can get the English version on the ELMO. And this would be page 2 of the English version on the ELMO, please. Mr. Rajic, I'm going to read a part of the top paragraph on page 2 of the English version. This is what it says: "This could also be a working meeting in which we seek to formulate a Croatian political strategy, an overhaul Croatian policy including that of the Bosnia-Herzegovina HDZ in the period ahead of us." Do you see that part on your version, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For you, it's on the page that bears the yellow tab number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to make a correction. The Prosecutor said yellow, and the interpretation was green.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have seen the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Simply, my question to you sir is whether, in fact, what is being said here, or the purpose of this meeting is one in which you, other members of your delegation from Bosnia-Herzegovina, together with President Tudjman, sought to discuss and arrive at an overall policy that would apply to Croats found not only in Croatia but also in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, once again, I have to voice my reservation with regard to the content which this material features. However, in my recollection, we talked about the difference of opinions which existed within the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and which did not only have to do with the strategy and the policy but also with the daily operational implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajic. The usher, I just noticed the passage that I've just referred to is not shown on the television. I'm talking about the very top paragraph on the page. That's it. Beginning with the words, "It seems to me." Mr. Rajic, did you and other members of your delegation look to President Tudjman as someone who could resolve the differences that existed between the members of your own delegation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed that President Tudjman can and is willing to help to overcome those issues which, in our political work, cropped up, or at a sporadic level, but also in terms of questions of substance. I believe that he could help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in terms of substance, perhaps one of the most significant substantive issues confronting your party at the time was the difference in opinion, the difference in policy, advocated on the one hand by Stjepan Kljujic and on the other hand by Mate Boban; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite my best effort, I really cannot recollect and make a distinction between Mr. Kljujic's and Mr. Boban's political views at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me direct you now to the yellow tab number 2, and in the English version we are looking at page 20.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel indicate the pages in the B/C/S version as well for the interpreters, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise. The B/C/S version, you will find it at ERN number 00850410. I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this portion, sir, relates to something I've asked you about before, that is the contours or the structure that Bosnia-Herzegovina ought to ultimately have, and on this page, President Tudjman is speaking, and he is -- let me just read part of this for you. Directing you to the part that you can follow along. "In addition, one of our people in Bosnia drafted a proposal for demarcation whereby the Croatian areas and those that you have included in the community of Herceg-Bosna and the community of Croatian Posavina, in the events of demarcation, Croatia would get not only those two communities but also, for geopolitical reasons, Kazinska and Bihacka Krajina which would satisfy almost ideally the Croatian national interests, not only present but also for the future. And then from the remaining areas where," and then it continues. And then just to continue briefly into the next paragraph, "And to create a statelet therefore out of the remaining part around Sarajevo where mostly Muslims and some Catholic Croats would stay, which would resemble the small historical land of Bosnia. It would therefore be a buffer zone in the demarcation of Serbia and Croatia, and in such conditions, it would have to rely on Croatia to a large extent." Now, continuing on to page 21 of the English version. Mr. Rajic, I'm going to move down two paragraphs, three paragraphs. "It seems to me therefore that just as we have taken advantage of this historic moment to establish an independent, internationally recognised Croatia, I believe that it is time we take the opportunity to gather the Croatian people inside the widest possible borders." Now, sir, do you recall that President Tudjman --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise but I couldn't follow you. Could I be given the number and identification in Croatian again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I'm on your page, sir. You would be looking in the vicinity of -- the usher might assist you in locating what we call the ERN number; the last four digits would be 0410. And then continuing on to 0411. Beginning with the words, "It seems to me, therefore..."

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is pages in B/C/S 410 to 413, end of page 410 onward.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You've got it now? Okay. The second passage, shall I read it again or would you like to read it to yourself beginning with the words, "It seems to me, therefore..."

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need for to you do this. I read it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, my questions are are those the words of President Tudjman describing an objective ultimately to expand the borders of an internationally recognised Croatia, squeezing the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina back toward Sarajevo as a way to bring a greater number of Croats together in one state?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I said it before, and you can put this question to me a thousand times, yet I will respond in the same manner. I cannot accept this document as an authentic document. And I can only comment on it with the reservation by saying, should this prove to be an authentic document, that is as far as that is concerned. As far as your question goes, I think that the methodology of quotations taken out of context serves its purpose and complex, multi-layered questions cannot end in another situation but to lead me to answer in quite different manners in connection with one and the same fact. I cannot do that. I'll explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you a couple of questions. This is a cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness be allowed to answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me to answer where I began?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, as I understand it, there is no question put forward by the Prosecution. So there is not answering the question. If you want to make some explanation of your stand, your views, on this very issue, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I understand the Prosecutor's statement as a question. If I'm wrong, I apologise to the Prosecutor and to you, Your Honours, but I don't think I'm wrong. I emphasised that the methodology of quotations taken out of context, should this turn out to be an authentic document, serves a purpose. I'm not clear why the section of the text was not read out in which President Tudjman says that given the statement made by General Kadijevic of the JNA, that he will accept a political solution, that a political division, a political solution in Bosnia-Herzegovina, could speed up the process of establishing the universal peace and peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mr. Tudjman, President Tudjman, also emphasises that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, about 1.4 million Serbs were living, that about 570.000 lived in Croatia, that the number shrank but that probably it shrank due to their transfer to Bosnia-Herzegovina and that more than 1.5 million people were present there. And then the conclusion is drawn on this basis which I think the Prosecutor skips out on purpose, namely that the existence of Bosnia-Herzegovina under current circumstances is such that we, that is the Croats, cannot advocate it, that we cannot put it as an open question, and why not accept the offer of demarcation when this is in the interest of both the Republic of Croatia and the Croat people in Croatia and the Croat people in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Furthermore, it is said here, particularly due to the fact that on many occasions, he spoke about this both with Izetbegovic and Milosevic. So, Your Honours, had the Prosecutor read out the entire text, then his conclusion could have been quite a different one. This is why I asked for your advice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you may not be familiar with the proceedings before this Tribunal. During the direct or cross-examinations, the party is entitled to ask you the questions which is relevant to this case. I think under the obligation, you are obliged to answer those questions with a very simple answer, that is yes or no. If you need some explanation to your answer, you may do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor will ask you several questions concerning this issue. You may listen to his question, answer it. If you need, you may offer some explanations on that. That's the procedure Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. before this Tribunal. Mr. Stringer, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to follow up on a couple of the comments that you just gave us, Mr. Rajic. First of all, you made reference to this part concerning an offer of demarcation. You're referring to an offer of demarcation that came or was communicated by General Kadijevic; is that correct, a general of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. General Kadijevic, according to statements made by Kljujic, said that the JNA would embrace a political solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. A political solution involving an offer of demarcation to use the words that you just gave us a moment ago, an offer of demarcation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the statement made by Kadijevic, as this was conveyed to me by Mr. Kljujic, this cannot be concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you -- I'm using your words, an offer of demarcation. That was the explanation that you gave and I'm just trying to clarify that. Was there some sort of an offer coming from the Serb side that related to demarcation or redrawing of boundaries as part of a political solution between Croats and Serbs? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what I was talking about. A political division was not proposed by Kadijevic, according to Mr. Kljujic as it is said in this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: One other question, then we'll move on to the next thing. This meeting is taking place in December of 1991 in Zagreb. Croatia has been at war. The war is very soon to come to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Isn't it true, sir, that President Tudjman saw all of these events, both political and military, as providing an opportunity to gather people, Croatian people, inside the widest possible borders? Wasn't that his view? That all of these events provided an opportunity for territorial, if you will, reconciliation of a greater number of Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, but Mr. Tudjman, as a statesman and politician of major scope, also spoke about the possibilities that had existed in our land. Let me repeat it. Conditional sentences and ideas were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me direct you to what has been marked as tab number 3 on the document in front of you. The English version, page 28.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It should be your tab number 3, which would be at page 00850442. Tab number 3. On this part, Mr. Rajic, another person present at the meeting is talking named, Miro Lasic. Do you recall that Miro Lasic was there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is what he says: "I am personally happy and proud for having lived through these historic events and having taken part in them under President Tudjman's leadership, so the creation of a Croatian state is the essence." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the very bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, was Mr. Lasic, Miro Lasic, a member of your delegation from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all one delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And your delegation was all under the leadership of President Tudjman, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Under the leadership of President Kljujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So Miro Lasic was wrong in this statement?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he was flattering the President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And he was also incorrect in his assertion that the Croatian -- the creation of a Croatian state is the essence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know all that Mr. Lasic said on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Wasn't it true, sir, that on that point he was speaking on your behalf, the behalf of other members of your delegation who shared the same view?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was mandated to speak on anybody's behalf. We were all politically committed and the offices we held did not prevent anyone from voicing his own opinion, if he wanted to do so. And instead of my having to answer as to what Mr. Lasic said or did not say, I'd be happier if you asked me about what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to tab 4 and we will talk about what you said. Tab 4 on your document, English page 36, B/C/S, 00850437. Now, Mr. Rajic, you might want to go back a couple of pages to find the part where you actually begin talking. I can represent to you that what's on the page I've directed you to is attributed to you in this document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've found the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now, if you would move forward to the page where the tab number 3 is found, that's the page where I'm going to -- I'm sorry, tab 4, tab 4. This is what you said: "As long as a sovereign Bosnia exists, yes, but when it is attacked and others start carving it up, not us first, we know then what our historical right is. In this context, I would like to say that we cannot accept those claims which proceed from the notion that the current ethnic picture in Herceg-Bosna is the relevant factor according to which everything will be decided. We are proceeding from the historical right of the Croatian people, from the statehood which existed in 1939, as a minimum, and from looking at the ethnic picture in continuity." Now, Mr. Rajic, I've got one question and then I give you the floor to explain what you're talking about here, but I want to suggest to you that what you're referring to in 1939 is the state of the Hrvatska Banovina that existed for a short period of time just prior to and during World War II, and that that statement on your part is an indication of an objective to re-establish or to at least look to the Banovina as a starting point from which Croatian territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina would be established. Would you agree with that, sir, or do you want to explain your own views in respect of the Banovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply cannot agree with your reinterpretation of what I said. So everything is taken out of context. In this part, in this segment, I'm saying that those claiming that there has been radical change in the conduct of the party politics are not right, that is that this change took place in Zagreb. And that the concept of a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina was abandoned, and this objection -- these objections create a confusion, disinformation and that it needs clearing up. And then we come to what you quoted, where you say that there has been no radical change because even the declaration of the programme said, and I'm quoting here, "The declaration of the programme," not myself. And then the text comes which was taken over from the declaration or statement of the programme, of the HDZ as such, as whole. That the HDZ supports, endorses, the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but if and when it is attacked, and when others start carving up its territory and we never, as the first, then we know what our historical right is. So if you look at this statement together with the introductory part then the conclusion is completely different and that is no announcement of any measures like the establishment of a state in the territory of the erstwhile Banovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is a meeting taking place in December of 1991. Let me suggest to you, sir, that by the end of 1992, say by the time just before the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was announced in January, 1993, that in that period of time, in fact, the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina was in great doubt, Serbs had achieved taking of approximately two-thirds of the territory of the country and in fact others had started to carve up such that by the end of 1992, your policy and the policy of your party was to take advantage of the opportunity to create a Croatian state as President Tudjman has described earlier in this transcript.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, sir, if you changed the years deliberately. 1991 and 1992. So will you please try to help me to get my bearings in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll try and break that down. That was a bad question from me. If I understand correctly what you're saying is that the possibility of a demarcation, an expansion of Croatian borders, was only something that would be considered in the event that a carve up of Bosnia-Herzegovina was already under way, perhaps started by others. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I merely reinterpreted the programme of the Croat Democratic Union so this is not my personal position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was the position of the Croatian Democratic Union as of the end of 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That remained the policy in place at the end of 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this policy is still in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: By the end of 1992, the situation was such that your party, under the leadership of President Tudjman, deemed it a good opportunity to proceed with that policy of an expansion of Croatian borders, establishment of a greater Croatian state, along the lines of the Banovina, by the end of 1992. That was the policy, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To begin with, and again I must say I have my reservations regarding the authenticity of this document. In late 1992, the situation was completely different, and it is not consistent with this act. I don't understand the question, because now we are in 1991, now we are in 1992, and both times at the end of the respective years. So I'm rather confused, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Maybe the next passage will help clear it up. Let's move to tab number 5 on your document, English page 56, bottom of the page, B/C/S page 00850478. This is President Tudjman talking, saying, "Therefore the survival of Bosnia-Herzegovina as an independent and sovereign state, even if possible, is in any case against the interests of the Croatian people and makes impossible the normal territorial establishment of the Croatian state and creates conditions for the disappearance of what remains of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina today." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you were in this meeting, sir, did you share his view that an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina was contrary to the interests of your people in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that Mr. Tudjman said it as it says here. Besides, you omitted a very important sentence at the very bottom. If we take this statement such as it is written. And it says, "Moreover, an integral, united Bosnia and Herzegovina is no more today because there was war in Croatia and the Serbs had seceded and taken away 70 per cent of the territory." But if you, Mr. Prosecutor, are interested in my attitude, in my attitude to these facts why don't you let me read the text, which I did not dispute, which I indeed said so that this Honourable Chamber could decide -- could judge my own participation, my own role in all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you've told us that President Tudjman was the leader of your party and that you were a member of a delegation that went to meet with him twice, once in June of 1991, once in December of 1991. Now, on the basis of that, sir, I'm trying to question you about your views and the extent to which they were consistent with the views being expressed by other members of your delegation, as well as those being expressed by President Tudjman. That's what's of interest to me. So with respect, I don't want to limit my questions only to what you said, because it's helpful to us and I believe to the Trial Chamber for them to have your views on what's being said by other political leaders of the HDZ and that's why I'm asking you about some of these other statements that are being made. If you don't share the views that are expressed by the others, then tell us. That's what we want to know.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Prosecutor. I said that I did not believe the content of the quoted passage that you have just quoted. I do not think that President Tudjman could have put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's move to the next item, which is tab number 5B, English page 60, B/C/S 00850485.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is again President Tudjman speaking. "I've written down somewhere the date when we discussed how talks should be held with both sides and our aim, our aim from the beginning, from the proclamation we issued, if you want, was not to preserve Bosnia and Herzegovina as it is today. Essentially, this is not in the interests of Croatian policy, as Croatian policy would, in this way, be permanently frustrated by the demographic and territorial loss in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, we finally wanted and it was no accident that in the preamble to the Croatian constitution, we also mention the Banovina of Croatia." So, sir, my question, then, is, as the President and leader of the HDZ party in both Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, was it not President Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Tudjman's view that the boundaries of the Banovina should be re-established, that the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as they existed at that time, should be reduced and pushed back towards Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. President Tudjman did not ask for that, and you cannot read that into the text. If this is correct, then one can see that President Tudjman is saying something which is completely opposite to that, which in no way does not jeopardise the -- prejudice the idea of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Quite the reverse. That it is not our aim to preserve Bosnia-Herzegovina as it is today. How will the Croatian people as a whole accept that Bosnia-Herzegovina at the end of 1991 in which the Serbs had appropriated 70 per cent of the territories and were threatening us with slaughter and expulsion? If you are trying to incriminate that particular fact in Tudjman's speech, then I cannot agree with you. He is simply linking up to what was said earlier, as it says here and again I have my reservations, that in the preamble there is an invitation of the Croatian state that is the Croatian constitution, and there is a mention of -- a reference to Banovina knowing that somebody will want to appropriate Bosnia-Herzegovina and give the Croats a one-way ticket into their world. That is the gist of what President Tudjman said on countless occasions, not only at this meeting. I heard it from him on many occasions before and after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, is it your testimony, then, that the reference to the Banovina in these documents, including your own reference to 1939, is not an indication that ultimately, your objectives, your desires, were to re-establish in Bosnia-Herzegovina territories formerly falling within the Hrvatska Banovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, thank you, at long last I get a question that I wanted to hear. References to Banovina Hrvatska and President Tudjman and Boban and Kljujic's and my words have absolutely nothing to do with the establishment of a state in that territory, or with intent to annex that territory to the Republic of Croatia. The message there is completely different that Bosnia and Herzegovina is also the Croatian land, and that nobody can count on Bosnia-Herzegovina without Croats in it as one of the three pillars which must underpin it. That is Mr. Prosecutor, the purpose, the raison d'etre for all the mentions and reinterpretations of the phenomenon of the Banovina Hrvatska of 1939. That is how I always saw this interpretation, and I'm still loyal to it. Nobody can take Bosnia-Herzegovina without asking Croats, among others, what will be with it. That is the fundamental message.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, then am I correct that it was not your position, the position of others of your delegation, your leadership, that the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna should become part of Croatia? That was not your -- that was not the objective of your party?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the objective either of our party or the Croat community Herceg-Bosna, but we had -- we did not renounce our right that if our survival were threatened and if our right were in peril, we -- to look for our place under the sun in another way. And in case of a -- in case of a disintegration of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we'd rather go to our mother state than stay under the Serb occupation. If that is how we understand the gist of the discussion, then we shall arrive at a completely different conclusions. And let me I sure you, Mr. Prosecutor, because I was a witness to those events, I was an actor in them, it is very hard for me to listen to reinterpretations which are not consistent with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've got a couple more questions. I think we should be able to finish with the transcript today, just so you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you've already mentioned, we discussed briefly, the Tomislavgrad meeting which took place on the 27th of December, 1991. I'm going to refer to page 12 of the English. I've got just a couple of points on this and then we will be finished, Mr. President. Mr. Rajic, for you I would direct you to tab 7, yellow tab number 7. It's at the front part of the document. I think you said already you remember that the minutes of this meeting were read out to President Tudjman by Mr. Kostroman during your meeting in Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so what's being read out then are the minutes of the meeting which took place in Tomislavgrad on the 23rd of December, 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but I also said that according to my criteria, it was not done well, either linguistically or politically.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were present at this meeting in Tomislavgrad?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were acting as a vice-president of the HDZ, looking now at the top of page 12.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not the vice-president of the HDZ at the time. I was the President of the municipal board of Kupres HDZ and vice-president of the Presidency of the Croat community Herceg-Bosna, not the party's vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you were vice-president. And I believe, sir, moving to the end of this document, that you signed these minutes --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I wasn't the vice-president of anything. I was the vice-president or deputy president of the Presidency. I have to explain the difference. The -- because the vice-president is a collective office and the president is the individual office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that it indicates simply Bozo Rajic, vice-president? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, but then it says that this is the session of the Presidency of the HZ HB, and so when it says vice-president, yes, I'm the vice-president of the Presidency and then it is not incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I continue for a couple of minutes or do we have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to stop because there is a trial in here this afternoon. We have to be punctually on time. So we will resume tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 12.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 11th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 25
